name: Muddy Waters
hook: A Mississippi blues singer who plugged in when he moved to Chicago, and gave the Rolling Stones their name.

blurb.age13: Muddy Waters was born McKinley Morganfield in Mississippi in 1913 and grew up on a cotton plantation. In 1941 the folklorist Alan Lomax recorded him for the Library of Congress. In 1943 he moved to Chicago, like millions of Black Southerners leaving the South for factory jobs, and started playing electric guitar in loud city clubs. His records for the Chess brothers' label, from 1948, made the Chicago blues sound, and a British band named themselves the Rolling Stones after one of his songs.
blurb.adult: Born in Issaquena County, Mississippi, in 1913, and raised on the Stovall plantation near Clarksdale, where Alan Lomax recorded him for the Library of Congress in August 1941. He moved to Chicago in 1943 as part of the Great Migration, working factory jobs by day. Playing electric was partly practical: an acoustic guitar is hard to hear in a crowded bar. 'I Can't Be Satisfied' and 'I Feel Like Going Home' (Aristocrat, 1948, the label the Chess brothers renamed Chess in 1950) were his first hits, and by the early 1950s his band included Little Walter, Jimmy Rogers, Otis Spann and Willie Dixon. He died in 1983.
